filed by the police with regard to the accident occurred on 21.05.2021 in which injured Jugnu (hereinafter referred to as 'petitioner') suffered injuries.

Copy of DAR was supplied to petitioner as well as to Dalbir Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 1'), Joginder Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 2') and Bajaj Allianz General Ins. My issue-wise findings are as under:-
 ISSUE No.1:
Whether injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 21.05.2021 at 7.30 p.m. at Ram Murti Pasi Marg between Gate No.2 & 3, near Adventure sports Mall Sec-11, Rohini,
Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle i.e. car bearing registration no. DL10CT 1190 by respondent no. 1 (Dalbir Singh)?

OPP. 
As stated above, petitioner / injured has died during the pendency of the case but to prove that deceased petitioner suffered injuries due to this accident, on account of rash and negligence, on the part of respondent no. 1, Ms. Laxmi, widow of deceased petitioner, being an eye-witness of accident,
examined herself as PW1 and tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A.

PW1 deposed that on 21.05.2021 at about 07.30 P.M. she was sitting in e-rickshaw bearing no. DL-11EA-3518 along with her husband Jugnu (deceased petitioner), as a passengers and were going to their residence Kirari, Suleman Nagar from E.S.I. Hospital Sector 15, Rohini after meeting their neighbour /patient Madhu who was admitted in the E.S.I. Hospital and Kishor Paswan (injured in another connected case) was driving the said e-rickshaw very carefully at normal speed by following all traffic rules and regulations on extreme left side of the road and when e-rickshaw reached at Rammurti Passi Marg, Sector-11 Rohini, between gate no. 2 and 3 Adventure Sports Mall, suddenly a car bearing No. DL-10CT-1190 came from back side in rash, negligent and zigzag manner with uncontrolled high speed and without following the traffic norms first hit our E- rickshaw from back side by its front left side then a green colour three wheeler goods carrier bearing no. DL-ILZ-4871 and thereafter hit a pedestrian with great impact.

PW1 further deposed that the impact was so powerful that E-rickshaw and three wheeler goods carrier both overturned and they all sustained grievous injuries They were immediately removed to Bhagwan Mahavir Hospital, Pitampura for treatment.
PW1 further deposed that above accident took place due to sole rash, negligent and Jugnu Vs. Dalbir Singh & Ors.

sentences.text: In her cross examination, by Ins. Co., no suggestion put to PW1 regarding the manner in which the accident had occurred.

Nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1, as far as negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 is concerned, as being injured PW1 is natural eye-witness of accident and respondent no. 1 has not at all cross examined the PW1.

Further,
respondent no. 1, being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence.

Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case, meaning thereby that respondent no. 1 has nothing to say about the rash and negligence on his part and the manner in which the accident had occurred as deposed by the PW1.
Further, the DAR shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/337/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner (since deceased) suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his MLC filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

Relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh,
Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under:-

entities.text:
Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh,
Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.
This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation if so, what amount and from whom of respondents?

OPP. 
10.

As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured, petitioner (since deceased) and now his legal heirs are well within their rights to claim compensation from the respondents on pecuniary heads.

Accordingly,
the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.

Now, the second part of the issue in hand with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
11.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009), held as under: -
"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

14.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas and has not filed any legal offer.

However, as stated above, one of the connected case has already been settled by the Ins. Co., whcih inter alia means that Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and hence, merely taking technial pleas, that too without any supporting evidence, insurnce company cannot escape from its liabilities.

In view of the above discussion, since the respondent no.3 / Ins.
Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner /
insured and to pay compensation to the claimants.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further,
respondent no. 1, being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence.
Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case, meaning thereby that respondent no. 1 has nothing to say about the rash and negligence on his part and the manner in which the accident had occurred as deposed by the PW1.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.
This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered injuries in the said accident.
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured, petitioner (since deceased) and now his legal heirs are well within their rights to claim compensation from the respondents on pecuniary heads.
Accordingly,
the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
However, considering the treatment record, it is presumed that some amount must have been spent on the treatment of petitioner, a lump sum amount of Rs. 10,000/- is allowed to claimants towards medical expenditure.
Further,
considering the hospitalization and a number of visits to hospital, an amount of Rs.
10,000/- is awarded to the claimants towards conveyance charges and considering the nature of injuries, it is presumed that victim must have taken special diet for his speedy recovery and hence, seeing the nature of injuries suffered by the victim, it is presumed that petitioner must have spent some amount towards special diet and hence, a sum of Rs.10,000/- for special diet is granted to the claimants.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, as stated above, one of the connected case has already been settled by the Ins. Co., whcih inter alia means that Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and hence, merely taking technial pleas, that too without any supporting evidence, insurnce company cannot escape from its liabilities.
